properties.name: A proposed change can be read as a delta before it lands
properties.statement: A pull request is a delta that has not happened yet. For a project under design control, the design must be able to read a candidate change (a PR branch, a patch) the same way delta reads a landed one — which artifacts would drift, and which capabilities, interfaces and requirements those artifacts realize (propagate from the touched set) — but STRICTLY READ-ONLY: a review reports what the change would mean to the design and never writes an accept, because accepts record what IS, and a PR is not yet. When the PR touches a published or consumed interface, the report must say so by name, because that is the part of the diff a reviewer cannot see from the code alone. Anthony's scenario, 2026-07-28: at his job (a founding site of the Bluesky project, blueskyproject.io), 'just today I got a request to review a PR on bluesky-httpserver — delta would see the difference between the current version and what the PR adds/changes.' The cross-repo half of his scenario — bluesky-httpserver is tightly coupled with bluesky-queueserver; does the PR affect the other repo? — is deliberately NOT this requirement: it is the standing composition thread (req:seam-incompatibility, req:composed-analysis, dec:linked-repos-poc), where the delta review's touched-interface list becomes the input to a seam check against the coupled design's mirrored surface.
